answers: We're Golden Valley Reefer, a refrigerated truckload carrier (trucking / freight) out of California's Central Valley. We haul fresh produce — lettuce, strawberries, grapes, citrus — from Salinas and Fresno to big distribution centers. We sell by the load: one full reefer truckload, priced per load.

Our lanes: Salinas, CA to Chicago IL (about 2,130 miles), Atlanta GA (about 2,450), Dallas TX (about 1,640) and New York NY (about 2,950). Fresno, CA to Chicago (about 2,000), Atlanta (about 2,300), Dallas (about 1,480) and New York (about 2,800). All reefer equipment. Right now it's spring produce bid season, so shippers are locking in contracts.

Carrier cost per mile runs roughly $2.30 to $2.70 depending on the lane — these are illustrative estimates, not audited numbers. Longer East Coast runs are cheaper per mile (New York around $2.30, Atlanta $2.40), Chicago about $2.50, and the shorter Dallas runs cost more per mile, around $2.70. Fresno lanes are about five cents a mile cheaper than Salinas. Fuel is the other big driver — use the standard diesel surcharge your engine already applies.

Three customer tiers: STANDARD for new or spot shippers, PREFERRED for repeat produce growers, STRATEGIC for our big grocery-chain contracts. Example customers (make them fictional): a grocery chain we'd call Harvest Table Markets (STRATEGIC), Sierra Sun Growers (PREFERRED), Bluebonnet Fresh Distributors (PREFERRED), Lakeshore Produce Co. (STANDARD), and Peachtree Greens (STANDARD).

Margins: STANDARD target 32%, minimum 14%, never below 7%. PREFERRED target 30%, min 12%, absolute min 6%. STRATEGIC target 26%, min 9%, absolute min 5%. Reefer has more risk (claims, temperature), so we keep a bit more margin than dry van. Your defaults for counter buffer and max rounds are fine.

We'll trade price for: 12-month contracts (worth about 4 points of margin to us), volume of 30 or more loads a week (about 3 points), a 48-hour pickup window so we can plan around harvest timing (about 2 points), and NET15 payment (about 1 point). We do NOT want NET60 — it should cost the buyer about 2 points. Some shippers ask for drop trailers at the farm; we can't price that today.

Auto-approve deals up to $3 million in total contract value; anything above that a person on our team signs off. Tone for the sales agent: warm, plain-spoken and fast — like a dispatcher who knows produce. Mention cold-chain reliability and on-time delivery, never pushy, never fluffy.
